subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient gain an opt-in reconnect attempt ceiling, and which callers should use it while node-host keeps unlimited recovery?
rationale: The source-level unbounded scheduler is real, but the existing node-host contract intentionally relies on indefinite reconnects, so the retry policy cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Opt-in cap for short-lived callers
options.body: Keep the default unlimited for node-host, add a package-level maxReconnectAttempts option, and wire only maintainer-approved CLI/SDK/probe callers after real reconnect proof.

options.title: Global default cap
options.body: Set a default retry ceiling for every GatewayClient user, accepting the upgrade risk that long gateway outages can strand node-host clients until an external supervisor restarts them.

options.title: No retry ceiling
options.body: Leave reconnect attempts unlimited and instead focus follow-up work on listener cleanup, diagnostics, and clearer reconnect-paused events.

recommendation.title: Opt-in cap for short-lived callers
recommendation.body: Keep the default unlimited for node-host, add a package-level maxReconnectAttempts option, and wire only maintainer-approved CLI/SDK/probe callers after real reconnect proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to steipete for the original Gateway WebSocket control plane and current package-client ownership, making this the best available policy-routing owner.
